note:
**Coverage.** Forty-three physical pages, twenty measured regions on twelve of them, all
accounted once: eight figure rows, five table rows and seven excluded regions. Sixteen
exhibits are captioned, thirteen of them own a row and Table 3 owns nothing.

**The paper pastes instead of typesetting.** Six of the twenty regions are images of the
paper's own equations: p7 holds (1) and (2) with the sentence 'we can calculate r more
accurately by' cut off above them; p9 holds two whole paragraphs plus (4) and (5) - the
Manhattan distance and the infinity-norm distortion - so the text layer jumps straight
from 'after some original improvements' to 'By the above improvements' and two paragraphs
exist only as pixels; p11 holds (6) under the words 'Therefore, we have' and (7) with its
own lead-in sentence under the 3.4 heading. A reader can only recover those paragraphs by
OCR, and a census that trusted the text layer would report a paper with no derivation.

**One page is a screenshot of a page.** p19 is a 617x707 px image of a fully typeset text
page - prose, displays (8), (9), (10), the spectral-decomposition radical, the diagonal
matrix D, the four-node transition matrix with decimals and the ergodic vector
[0.18749998 0.24999998 0.31249997 0.24999998]. Its text layer is empty, its running head
is absent, and the region pass sees one 487 pt box. This is the extreme case of the
apparatus limit recorded in the last two checkpoints: the census is measuring the page's
composition, not the paper's content, and here the whole content of a page is a picture.

**Three captions live on their own pages.** p10, p25 and p29 carry no image, no drawing,
no running head and no body text - only the caption line under the resale banner. In each
case the artwork sits on
the previous page (Figures 2, 9, 10). A page-turn rule that assumed 'caption and artwork
share a page' would lose three of eight figures here, and a 'the last region before the
caption' rule would still be right - but only because each page has a single region.

**Caption geography.** All eight figure captions print below the art, all five table
captions above their grid, and the two kinds never mix. Table gaps are 12 to 16 pt from
the caption's last line to the top rule; figure gaps are 2 pt for Figure 1 and 1.5-2 pt
for Figures 3 and 4, which is tight enough that a 3 pt shave of the region box would weld
caption to artwork. The two welded double captions (p20 'Figure 5: ... Figure 6: ...' and
p24 'Figure 7: ... Figure 8: ...') are single text units, and in both cases the paper
used one image for two numbered exhibits.

**Table drafting is the plainest in the block.** Four of five grids are three rules and
nothing else - no verticals, no side frames, no stripe, no merged cell - so a reader sees
a header band and rows with no column guides at all. Table 1 spills 32 pt past the right
margin and Table 6 spills 9 pt, and those are the only two overflows in the document. The
one modern-looking grid, Table 6, is also the only one with merged cells on both axes and
the only one whose frame visibly overruns the text block. Nobody aligns on the decimal
point; Table 5 looks aligned only because its four counts all carry three decimals.

**The citation habit is unlabelled.** Not one exhibit in forty-three pages is named by
number. The body points with 'the table below', 'the picture below', 'as the chart
shown', 'as in the pictures shown below', and five of thirteen rows are pointed at that
way; the other eight are never referenced. A cross-reference extractor would return
nothing for this paper, and a 'how many figures does the text cite' metric would say a
paper with sixteen exhibits cites none - which is why mention style is recorded per row
rather than aggregated.

**Apparatus limits worth keeping.** The Chinese resale banner prints at the top of ALL
43 pages, text pages and image pages alike, so `caption_above` is that banner on every
page that opens with a box. p17 prints one line -
'Markov method' - as a heading on an otherwise empty page. p18's transition-matrix
displays are drawings that no region pass grouped. And the running heads stop at 'Page 25
of 25' while the file runs to 43 pages, so printed page number and physical page diverge
by up to 15 by the appendix.

rules: Twenty measured regions on twelve of forty-three pages resolve to THIRTEEN exhibit rows - eight figures and five tables - plus seven excluded regions, and every region is claimed exactly once [place.doc_order].

Thirteen of the twenty regions are exhibits; the other seven are not: four are pasted images of the paper's own equations or prose (pp7, p9 and p11 twice), one is a screenshot of a whole typeset page (p19), one is the Algorithm 1 block (p20) and one is a fragment of the Matlab appendix (p39) [geometry.family].

Sixteen exhibits are captioned - ten figures and six tables - but they resolve to thirteen rows because two of the captioned pairs share one pasted image each (Figures 5 and 6, Figures 7 and 8) and Table 3 owns no measured region at all [caption.verbatim].

Table 3 is the census's cleanest miss: the page carries three horizontal rules at y571.4, 592.8 and 642.1 pt, the rows print in two aligned columns 250 pt wide, and the region pass returned nothing for p13 - so the table is declared a gap rather than given an invented box [table.rule_style].

Three captions print on a page of their own: p10, p25 and p29 carry no image, no drawing, no running head and no body text - only the caption line and the resale banner. Two of those captions (Figures 2, 9) name artwork that sits on the PREVIOUS page; the third (Figure 10) names artwork that also sits on the previous page, so all three are recorded as captions below the art with a page of air between [caption.position].
Caption side is perfectly kind-driven and needs no exception: all eight figure rows carry their caption BELOW the artwork and all five table rows carry theirs ABOVE the grid [caption.position].
The gaps are tight and uniform for tables - 12 to 16 pt from caption to top rule across all five - while figures run from 2 pt (Figure 1) to 2 pt plus a page break [caption.verbatim].

Numbering is one spelling on all fourteen quoted captions - 'Figure N:' and 'Table N:', space after the label, colon after the number - and no caption anywhere deviates, which makes this the most regular caption set in the block [caption.numbering].

Captions are short bare noun phrases: three words at the minimum (Table 1), fifteen at the longest (Figure 9), one sentence each, and the two welded double captions (p20, p24) still count as one text unit each [caption.words].

No caption gives a unit, names a symbol, states a condition or draws a conclusion - voice `none` on all thirteen rows - so every decoding instruction lives in the prose or, in Figure 4's case, on the axes [caption.voice].

Family mix is thin and diagram-heavy: four line charts, two map-or-plan-view rows, one grouped bar chart and one scatter, and there is no 3-D, no histogram, no box-or-violin and no pie anywhere in forty-three pages [geometry.family].

Legends are split three ways: four rows carry none at all, three put theirs INSIDE the plot area in the upper-right corner (Figures 3, 4, 7/8), and one prints its key BELOW the axis (Figure 9) - the only below-plot legend in the block so far [geometry.legend].
No colourbar exists in the paper - not on the point cloud, not on the three map rows, not on the bar chart - so nothing in this census could be coded from a ramp [geometry.colorbar].

Two rows are composite panels and both come from a single pasted JPEG: Figure 5/6 is two Seoul basemaps split by a white gutter with no drawn rule, Figure 7/8 is two fully titled line panels, and in both cases the welded caption is the only thing that says which half is which [geometry.panel_count].

Neither the basemaps nor the point cloud is geographic despite their captions: the scatter in Figure 2 has no basemap, no coastline and no coordinates, and the two 'Plan' maps in Figure 5/6 carry no scale bar and no north arrow [geometry.family].
Printed numbers are axis furniture only - every chart in the paper ticks its axes except the point cloud, which ticks nothing - and no row puts a value on a mark [geometry.printed_numbers].

Four of the five grids use three rules and no verticals (top, under the header, bottom) - the plainest booktabs in the block - and only Table 6 is boxed, with a closed frame plus six vertical rules [table.rule_style].

Table 6 is also the paper's only grid with merged cells, and it merges on both axes: 'GDP per capita (USD)' across two columns, 'Standard' across two sub-rows and 'Density (mi2)' across three rows, which is why two of its horizontal rules stop halfway across the grid [table.merged_cells].
No grid is striped, none has a diagonal header cell and none continues across a page break - the block's most conservative table habit [table.zebra].

Units are printed inside the header on two of the five grids ('Capturing radius(km)', 'GDP per capita (USD)'), attached to a column name as 'Percentage(%)' on a third, and pushed into the row stub on Table 5 as 'num(million)' [table.units_in_header].

Grid size follows the data rather than a template: a twenty-symbol notation list (21x2), a five-row distribution (5x3), a three-row radius list (4x2), a transposed three-row time series (3x5) and a four-row country classification (4x4) [table.rows].

Widths run 364 to 457 pt against a 425 pt measure, and the two extremes overflow the text block - Table 1 by 32 pt and Table 6 by 9 pt - which are the paper's only two layout overflows anywhere [table.width].

Not one grid in the paper aligns its numbers on the decimal point: every numeric column is centred, and Table 5's four counts only LOOK aligned because they all print three decimals [table.decimal_aligned].

The citation habit is the weakest in the block: NO exhibit is named by number anywhere in forty-three pages, not once - the prose points at them with unlabelled phrases ('the table below', 'the picture below', 'as the chart shown') or not at all [mention.style].

Eight of the thirteen rows are pointed at, seven of them from the page they print on and Figure 4 one page early, introduced by 'connection between capturing area and charging station density is displayed in the picture below' [mention.lead_pages].
No exhibit is pointed at twice, and five rows are never referenced from the body at all: Figures 1 and 3, Table 2, Table 4 and Table 5 [mention.count].

Pages cluster their exhibits at the foot: eight of thirteen rows sit in the bottom third of their page, three at the top and two in the middle, and no exhibit comes close to taking a page - the largest row is Table 1 at 30 per cent and the mean is 14.8 per cent [place.area_frac].
Nothing is solo-page, and the two figures pasted into identical 432x347 pt boxes on consecutive pages (Figures 3 and 4) are the only rows that share a placement [place.solo_page].

Placement follows the task structure: the model half (2.2, 3.2, 3.3, 3.4) takes the notation table, Figure 1, the point cloud and Table 2, the results half (4.1, 4.3) takes Figures 3 to 9 with Tables 4 and 5, and the evaluation half (5.1, 5.2.2) takes Table 6 and Figure 10 [place.section_path].

Section kind is read off the heading, so eleven rows land in `other`, one in `symbols` and one in `evaluation` - no row is typed `result` even though eight of them report results, which is the same detector flatness the last two papers showed [place.section_kind].
Page order is crowded where the paper pastes: p15 carries a figure at the top and a table at the bottom, p24 carries a two-panel chart and a bar chart, and p26 carries two tables [place.page_order].

The paper's page count is not its physical page count: the running heads stop at 'Page 25 of 25' while the PDF runs 43 pages, because the screenshot pages (p19 above all) carry no running head at all [place.doc_order].
